When unsupervised metrics fail, active model selection offers a promising alternative by using labels for selection. Under a fixed budget, we compare training on all labels with unsupervised selection against splitting labels evenly between training and active selection (Table 3).

In unsupervised selection, methods may use the programs’ predictions and extracted features to estimate their relative performance. In active selection, methods additionally have access to a limited annotation budget and may actively query labels to distinguish between candidate programs.
